title: Scalar and vector quantities (স্কেলার ও ভেক্টর রাশি)
placement: Book page 38, topic 2.3: স্কেলার ও ভেক্টর রাশি. Next to চিত্র ২.০৩ (vectors A, B, C, D), or in place of it.
description: Scalar and vector quantities (page 38, 2.3) as a game of finding a friend on a school field seen from slightly above. The student stands on a chalk compass (উ পূ দ প); the friend is hiding. One big numbered button leads five steps, and its same numbered badge rings what to touch on the field. 1. Call your friend: the answer gives a size only ("আমি ২৫ m দূরে"), a measuring line sweeps round and the whole ring of places 25 m away lights up with question marks, so the friend cannot be found; the rule: 25 m is a মান, and a quantity one value describes completely, like temperature (37° C, the book's example), is a স্কেলার রাশি, but a মান alone did not fix the friend's place. 2. Ask the direction too ("২৫ m, উত্তর-পূর্ব দিকে"): the compass point glows, one arrow A grows to exactly one place, the friend pops up and the student walks over: অবস্থান needs মান and দিক, a ভেক্টর রাশি (the book's sentence: শুধু দূরত্ব দিয়ে কাজ হয়নি, তার দিকটিও নির্দেশ করতে হয়েছিল). 3–5. The book's চিত্র ২.০৩ in the same story: B, C and D wait in turn at other places; each one sent is told its clue, walks it, and its arrow slides, unturned and unstretched, onto the tail the caption compares it with: B covers A exactly (হুবহু এক, যদিও ভিন্ন অবস্থানে), C has A's মান but another দিক (an orange arc), D has C's দিক but half its মান. One result line, one rule that grows to the caption's words and the book's lists (স্কেলার: তাপমাত্রা, সময়, দৈর্ঘ্য, ভর; ভেক্টর: অবস্থান, বেগ, বল). Distances are to scale (a 10 m bar lies on the grass); the children are drawn about five times bigger than life, and a note by the bar says so. Test tab: 5 questions on scenes set up for each (three flags with their distances, two of them 20 m away: where can Raju be; four flags 20 m away on the diagonals: which one is '20 m to the south-east'; why two arrows are different vectors; which of five arrows equals A; in the picture of the found friend, what the distance and A are, or what needs a direction too). Phone-first, Bangla.
